The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bdb2f21b345a4f0f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. statement: Fix the truncation b∗ selected in Section 3. There exist positive integers mi → ∞, tending p-adically to zero on the prescribed torsion branch, and theta forms Θi of weight (mi, mi, 1; −1) with the following simultaneous properties. (i) Their ordinary monomial-dual lattices have a uniform denominator bound, coefficientwise in the full tame group algebra and after every fixed truncated substitution used in the argument. One fixed scaling clears this bound. (ii) All constant Fourier–Jacobi coefficients tend to zero through degree b∗ − 1 of the tame variable, in compatible ordinary differential bases, uniformly at the boundary representatives. This is a full-ring estimate in Rb∗ . (iii) At augmentation, a nonconstant Fourier–Jacobi coefficient has an integral-frame evaluation of valuation bounded above by a constant independent of i. Thus the forms do not acquire unbounded common content. (iv) At both distinguished places above p, the fixed canonical (2, 1, 1) level is J and the operators p−2U2, p−2U3 have value 1. At every controlled upper (2, 2) place, including qi, the expanding center is invertible and the last binary spherical data are those of the final pair in (4.11). At the specified unramified Steinberg places the level is (3, 1) parahoric, without an additional refinement. All nonsplit finite places are hyperspecial. (v) At split good spherical places the Hecke parameters are (4.11) with η = Cmi νi. All constants may depend on the fixed original data, the fixed local tests and b∗, but not on i, qi, ni or the growing weights.
